$description: VoxClip design tokens. Source of truth for both apps. Generated outputs: apps/macos/Sources/VoxClip/Design/Tokens.swift, apps/windows/src/VoxClip.App/Themes/Tokens.xaml and apps/macos/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset/Contents.json (tools/design). Spec: doc/design.md section 16.

conventions.syntax: W3C Design Tokens group/token syntax ($type, $value, $description). Colour tokens are the exception: $value is a mode map {dark, light}.
conventions.system: A value of the form system:<name> means the platform colour named in $extensions.com.voxconvo.voxclip.macos / .windows; the generator must not substitute a hex value.
conventions.highContrast: windowsHighContrast names the WinUI SystemColor* resource used in the HighContrast theme dictionary. macOS relies on Increase Contrast and the system colours.
conventions.increaseContrast: A colour's increaseContrast {dark, light} (hex only) replaces its $value on macOS while Increase Contrast is on (the accessibilityHighContrast appearances). Only colours kept below a contrast minimum on purpose carry one; under Increase Contrast they must meet it. Windows uses windowsHighContrast.
conventions.units: Lengths are points on macOS and effective pixels (epx) on Windows. Durations are milliseconds.
conventions.platformValues: A dimension's $value is the macOS value; $extensions.com.voxconvo.voxclip.windows replaces it in Tokens.xaml only.
conventions.macosAsset: A colour whose extensions name macosAsset is also generated as apps/macos/Resources/Assets.xcassets/<name>.colorset (light for Any, dark for Dark).
conventions.source: Names the design-study token a colour's value comes from (Document <name>, or ADR-R29 <mockup name>).

window.$description: Behind content and sheets; same values as bg.sunken. v2 chrome: the Explorer, tab bar, right column, panels, timeline headers and the ruler inside In/Out. Windows: Mica shows through instead; use only as the Mica fallback colour.

surface.$description: Transcript page and other long-reading content surfaces. v2 editor: the transcript buffer, the active tab and the clip bar.

sunken.$description: Preview dock, timeline bed, Welcome side pane, empty-state cards. Same values as bg.window (v2 chrome).

elevated.$description: Caption tiles, popover fallback, onboarding cards, callout base.

muted.$description: Hover and pressed rows, skeleton bars, tile placeholders.

input.$description: Custom input backgrounds only: the Ask field, the command field and the Director composer (v2 raised). System text fields keep their own fill.

selectedRow.$description: Custom-drawn selected rows, pressed toggles and the on segment of a segmented control (v2 selrow). Native list selection keeps the system highlight. text.primary on it: dark 11.79:1.

default.$description: Hairline dividers: column splits, clip rows, inspector sections (v2 line). Decorative, so exempt from the 3:1 boundary minimum.

strong.$description: 3:1 boundaries: unselected clip rules, brackets and the transcript's ] glyph, suggestion outlines, drop-zone borders, the Windows splitter grip and flyout borders, and the edge of a custom surface made opaque under Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast. At least 3:1 against bg.surface, bg.sunken and bg.window in every appearance (dark 3.31:1 on bg.surface). The quiet v2 line2 is line.edge.

edge.$description: Input outlines and the timeline's top edge, its resize handle (v2 line2). Dark is a quiet 1.38:1 on bg.surface by design (impl-plan item 6): an input is identified by its bg.input fill and label, the edge by the panel under it and its resize cursor. Never for a mark or border that must read at 3:1; that is line.strong. Under Increase Contrast it is line.strong's value. Light is line.strong's value until the v2 light round.

primary.$description: Body text, Explorer rows, tabs, buttons and headlines (v2 t1). Contrast on bg.surface: dark 14.25:1, light 16.3:1.

secondary.$description: Labels, subtitles, secondary rows and icons, FX block labels (v2 t2).

muted.$description: Helper text, clip reasons, pause token text. Between text.secondary and text.tertiary, so the hierarchy stays monotonic; the study's pauseFg (#B0B2B8 / #55585F) was brighter than text.secondary. Contrast on pause.background: dark 5.28:1, light 5.16:1.

tertiary.$description: Meta text: section headers, meta lines, the status bar, notes and panel property labels (v2 t3, lifted from #717479 to reach 4.5:1). The lightest text step: dark 4.80:1 on bg.window and bg.sunken, 4.56:1 on bg.surface. Not for bg.elevated, bg.input or editor.band, where it is under 4.5:1.

disabled.$description: Disabled labels, keyboard hints and leading zero groups of timecodes (v2 t4). Exempt from contrast minimums: disabled, or a duplicate of a menu shortcut or a value read in full. Under Increase Contrast it reaches 4.5:1 on bg.window.

default.$description: Ink, the one accent, as a fill that carries text: prominent buttons, the selected choice, the selected clip's badge and the light playing word. Light is the icon tile's ink. Dark is a cool graphite, because macOS draws white on the AccentColor asset (sidebar selection, switches, checkboxes) and paper cannot carry white. The macOS AccentColor asset is generated from this token. On Windows App.xaml sets it as SystemAccentColorDark1 (light) and SystemAccentColor (both themes). accent.on on it: light 12.87:1, dark 4.78:1; white: light 13.55:1, dark 5.03:1.

pressed.$description: Pressed state of accent.default fills. Windows light SystemAccentColorDark2.

text.$description: Ink as text and marks on page, sunken and glass surfaces: rings, clip brackets and rules, the playhead, info icons and links. Light is text ink; dark is paper, which everything the app paints in dark inverts to, including the dark Export capsule (with word.playingForeground, 15.19:1). It equals text.primary, so links carry an underline. macOS DesignValues.accentText uses it while the system accent is the AccentColor asset and follows controlAccentColor otherwise. Windows dark SystemAccentColorLight2.

on.$description: Text and glyphs on accent.default and accent.pressed, matching the macOS system white on the accent. Contrast on accent.default: light 12.87:1, dark 4.78:1. Windows draws TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary from App.xaml instead.

soft.$description: Custom selection tint and the drop-target veil base: a light ink wash on paper, a dark paper wash on ink. text.primary on it: light 12.80:1, dark 10.38:1.

default.$description: VoxClip's own orange, used only where notes.md draws it: the playhead line and head, the timeline selection bar, and the one primary button per panel (with tint.on), set with an explicit tint. Never the system accent: accent.* stays Ink, so switches, checkboxes, list selection, focus rings and default buttons stay neutral (impl-plan item 10). Dark 5.57:1 on bg.surface and 6.19:1 on timeline.lane; light (provisional) 3.71:1 on bg.surface and 3.01:1 on timeline.lane.

pressed.$description: Pressed state of a tint.default fill. tint.on on it: dark 5.13:1, light 4.65:1.

on.$description: Label and glyphs on tint.default and tint.pressed: the primary button keeps a dark label in both appearances. Dark 6.21:1 on tint.default.

text.$description: The orange as a mark on content: the 2 x 19 pt transcript caret and selection edges. Dark equals tint.default; light is a darker text-safe orange (4.81:1 on bg.surface, 4.52:1 on editor.band).

selection.$description: Transcript text selection at text height, radius 2: tint.default at 16%. text.primary on it over editor.band: dark 10.60:1.

wash.$description: Selection wash over the timeline tracks: tint.default at 7%, no edges. Decorative; the ruler selection bar and the transcript selection carry it.

text.$description: Platform text selection: the macOS transcript and text fields on both platforms. Always the platform selection colour, which follows the Ink accent ramp.

transcript.$description: Transcript selection, drawn by the Windows app with text.primary on it (light 9.55:1, dark 5.33:1). Exactly the NSColor.selectedTextBackgroundColor macOS derives from the Ink AccentColor asset (measured in a bundled probe), so both platforms show the same grey wash. Never the playing-word fill. In High Contrast it is Highlight, so selected words use HighlightText.

text.$description: Transcript body inside the open clip (v2 text). Dark 11.42:1 on editor.band and 12.27:1 on bg.surface.

outside.$description: Transcript text outside the open clip (v2 out, lifted from #76797F so it reaches 4.5:1 on editor.band, where a clip boundary inside a paragraph puts out-of-clip words): dark 4.87:1 on bg.surface, 4.54:1 on editor.band.

gone.$description: Removed words under Show cuts (with a 1 pt strike in the same colour), pause lengths and folded commas (v2 gone, lifted from #64676D): dark 4.54:1 on editor.band, light 4.97:1.

playingBackground.$description: Fill behind the currently playing word (radius.xs, 2 pt inline padding). Light: the accent fill, ink. Dark: soft paper with ink text (Windows SystemAccentColorLight1), the reverse of the selection's polarity and calmer than full paper during playback. High Contrast keeps that reversal: WindowText with Window text, the inverse of body text, so the playing word never looks like the Highlight selection.

playingForeground.$description: Text of the playing word: paper on ink (light 12.87:1), ink on soft paper (dark 11.95:1). High Contrast: Window on WindowText, the theme's own body-text pair.

cut.$description: Text of cut words (still content, kept at >= 4.5:1). Also on pause.background behind a cut word that matches a search, so a step past the study's cutText: dark 5.6:1 on bg.surface and 4.73:1 on pause.background, light 5.28:1 and 4.62:1.

filler.$description: Suggested-filler dotted underline (macOS) and filler word text (Windows). Contrast on bg.surface: dark 8.3:1, light 5.2:1.

lowConfidence.$description: Dashed underline for low-confidence words (off by default).

correctionDot.$description: 2 pt dot under the first letter of a corrected word.

stroke.$description: Strikethrough line on cut words (macOS; Windows strikes in word.cut because XAML text decorations use the foreground). Contrast on bg.surface: dark 6.3:1, light 4.9:1.

fill.$description: Timeline hatch stripes for cut word ranges (2 pt stripes every 6 pt at 45 degrees). Contrast on timeline.track: dark 5.6:1, light 4.0:1.

pauseFill.$description: Timeline hatch stripes for cut pause ranges.

background.$description: Inline pause token and the collapsed '... 5 cut' token. Token text uses text.muted (dark 5.28:1, light 5.16:1).

band.$description: Band behind the lines of the open clip: from 8 pt above its first line to 8 pt below its last, full width. Light values are provisional until the v2 light mockup round (impl-plan 3.6).

text.$description: Gutter paragraph timecodes inside the open clip (SF Mono 11). A recorded exception to 4.5:1 (impl-plan item 6): dark 3.03:1 on editor.band, because the time duplicates what VoiceOver reads from the paragraph. Under Increase Contrast it reaches 4.5:1.

textOut.$description: Gutter timecodes outside the open clip. Decorative (impl-plan item 6); under Increase Contrast it reaches 4.5:1.

dot.$description: The 5 pt fold dot that stands for a run of removed words and pauses. Decorative: the fold reads as "1 cut: uh, pause 1.4 seconds" and the Cuts rotor lands on it. Hover draws it in text.secondary. Under Increase Contrast it reaches 3:1 on editor.band.

tint.$description: Words spoken by your AI voice, and nothing else: their tint behind the words at 16%, the A1 patch fill at 10%, and the gutter and Explorer waveform glyphs at full strength. Dark 6.36:1 on editor.band.

wave.$description: Waveform of an AI patch on the A1 lane, over ai.tint at 10%: #8FB3E8 at 85%. No outline.

add.$description: A proposed change not yet kept, and nothing else: hunk new words (19% behind the words), the 3 pt change bar, the ruler mark and the Outline dot. Dark 7.04:1 on editor.band.

warning.$description: Warning icons and text, slow states. Suggested fillers use word.filler.

warningBackground.$description: Custom warning callouts; Windows uses InfoBar severity colours instead.

dangerBackground.$description: Custom error rows and callouts; Windows uses InfoBar severity colours instead.

success.$description: Success icons and text. Always pair it with a symbol and words.

successBackground.$description: Custom success callouts; Windows uses InfoBar severity colours instead.

infoBackground.$description: Custom informational callouts; the info icon uses accent.text.

badgeBackground.$description: Neutral clip badge fill on the sidebar glass, bg.surface and bg.sunken: paper at 9% (dark), ink at 9% (light). Its numeral is text.secondary, at least 4.5:1 on all three; dark is 9% rather than the delta's 13%, which measures 4.2:1 on the sidebar glass. The selected clip's badge is the accent fill instead.

label.$description: The open clip's label colour (default "Paper"): the 2 pt range bar in the gutter, the 1.5 pt In/Out brackets on the ruler and the overview clip blocks (42% open, 24% others). Dark 9.53:1 on editor.band.

lane.$description: Timeline track lanes and the overview lane. Removed media in Source view is empty lane. Light values are provisional until the v2 light mockup round (impl-plan 3.6).

rulerOut.$description: The ruler outside In/Out, a step darker than bg.window; inside In/Out the ruler is bg.window.

piece.$description: 1 pt outline of V1 and A1 clip pieces. Decorative; a piece is identified by its fill, filmstrip or waveform.

seam.$description: The 1 pt cut seam through V1 and A1 in the Edited view. Decorative: cuts are also folds in the transcript, the Cuts rotor and the status summary.

track.$description: Track drawn on the bg.sunken timeline bed.

keptBackground.$description: Bed behind kept-speech waveforms on the track: paper at 9% (dark), ink at 7% (light).

waveform.$description: RMS waveform bars over kept speech (50 ms buckets, 2 px bars on a 3 px pitch): paper at 58% (dark), ink at 52% (light). At least 3:1 on timeline.keptBackground.

scopeDim.$description: Dims the track outside the selected clip: bg.sunken at 62% (dark), 66% (light). Off in High Contrast, where the brackets and trim handles mark the scope.

clipBracket.$description: The selected clip's 2 pt bracket line and end ticks above the track (accent.text). Unselected clips use line.strong; suggestions are dashed.

clipBand.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout. Band behind the active clip range: the accent at 12% (ink in light, paper in dark). Clip scope is now timeline.scopeDim.

stage.$description: Video surround in both appearances and in High Contrast. The only pure black allowed.

foreground.$description: Text and glyphs over video and the stage (transport pill, empty-stage label). The stage and its overlays stay dark in both appearances.

scrim.$description: REC pill and other chips drawn over video (78%).

transportOpaque.$description: Transport pill fill under Reduce Transparency (92%), with line.strong border.

drop.$description: 'Drop to transcribe' overlay background: bg.surface at 92%.

dropBorder.$description: 2 pt dashed border of the drop overlay (accent.text).

dropZoneBorder.$description: 2 pt dashed border of the Welcome drop zone: text.primary at 40%. Decorative; the zone's icon and label identify it.

mediaBackground.$description: Media stand-in chips over frames and cards: black 62% (design 5.4.8). One value in both appearances because chips sit on media.

mediaStroke.$description: 1 px inner line of a translucent media chip (design 5.4.8). Decorative.

mediaBackgroundOpaque.$description: Media chip fill under Reduce Transparency or with transparency effects off (design 5.4.8).

mediaStrokeOpaque.$description: 1 px inner line of the opaque media chip (design 5.4.8).

mediaForeground.$description: Media chip text and glyphs, the duration chip's numbers and the transcribing dots (design 5.4.4, 5.4.8).

warningGlyph.$description: Warning glyph on the corrupt-file chip: status.warning dark, used on media in both appearances (design 5.4.8).

progressTrack.$description: Track of the 2 px transcribing progress line along a tile's bottom edge: black 55%. Its fill is overlay.foreground (design 5.4.8).

rim.$description: 1 px inner rim of a media tile or thumbnail: white 10% (design 5.4.3, 5.4.5). Decorative.

sheen.$description: Peak of the loading sheen band: white 7.5% at 105 degrees, fading out on both sides (design 5.4.5). High Contrast draws no sheen.

ring.$description: Custom-drawn focus rings only (2 pt, offset 2), in accent.text. System controls keep the system ring / focus visual.

status.$description: Mono caps status labels (READY TO REVIEW style), gutter labels.

transcript.$description: Transcript page in the system font (SF Pro; Windows Segoe UI Variable Text) at 19/32 on both platforms. Zoom 13-28 pt (macOS) / 13-28 epx (Windows) in steps of 1; line height = size x 32/19.

timecode.$description: Gutter timecodes and timeline labels, m:ss.d.

fontFiles.$description: Brand fonts for rendered video only (captions and the AI MODIFIED label) under ADR-R29: the UI uses system fonts, and the apps stop loading these for UI with the old layout. Files live in shared/fonts/<family>/ with entries in shared/fonts/fonts.json, added through tools/captions/font-sources.json like the caption fonts. 'present' records whether the file is bundled as of 2026-10-25. Until a file is present the apps use the platform fallback named here, so nothing depends on a missing file.

xs.$description: Badges, chips and the playing-word fill.

control.$description: Buttons, the timeline track and the cut pause chip.

pane.$description: The video stage, sidebar selection, the selection bar, cards, thumbnails and callouts.

sheet.$description: Sheets and the whole-window drop overlay.

sm.$description: Pause and collapsed-cut tokens, keycaps, number badges.

lg.$description: Video stage, caption tiles. macOS 26: .containerConcentric with this as fallback.

hatchStripe.$description: Stripe width; stripe period 6, angle 45 degrees.

durationFast.$description: Strike draw-in, Pop caption preview, selection fill.

transportFadeDelay.$description: Transport pill fades after this much playback without pointer over the video (never under Reduce Motion).

spring.$description: SwiftUI .spring(response:dampingFraction:). Windows uses easeOut over durationSlow.

reduceMotion.$description: Every UI animation becomes instant under Reduce Motion (macOS accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion, Windows UISettings.AnimationsEnabled == false). Export output is unaffected.

transcriptMeasureMax.$description: About 72 characters at the default size.

sidebar.$description: Explorer pane width, its 1 pt divider after it: 224 by default and resizable 220-320 on macOS (v2 notes.md section 1; kept in ui.layout.explorerWidth after a divider drag), NavigationView OpenPaneLength 264 on Windows until WV1.

rightColumn.$description: Right column pane (title row, viewer, panel), its 1 pt divider before it. macOS default width = ideal + (window width - 1280) x 0.25 within min-max, narrowed toward min so the transcript keeps its minimum beside the Explorer: 404 at 1280 and 444 at 1440 (v2 notes.md section 1; kept in ui.layout.rightWidth after a divider drag). Windows until WV1: ideal - (1440 - window width) x 0.25, 388 at 1440 and 348 at 1280.

stagePortraitMax.$description: Largest 9:16 stage on both platforms; 1:1 is at most 320 high. The caption gallery scrolls below it.

inspector.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

timelineTrackHeight.$description: The whole track height is the scrub target.

selectionBarHeight.$description: Transcript selection bar: 36 (macOS glass bar), 40 (Windows CommandBarFlyout).

footerStatusHeightWindows.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

transportPillHeight.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

captionTileAspect.$description: Caption gallery tile height over width. Two tiles per row: width = (column - 8) / 2, height = width x 0.45.

welcomeWindow.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

breakpointThreeColumn.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout. Window width at or above which the inspector shows by default.

breakpointStack.$description: Below this width the preview stacks above the transcript (max 40% of the window height).
